 Results in a layered, fruit-driven cup with cocoa depth and refined sweetness. 
 Espresso 
 
 
 Dose: 18 g 
 
 
 Yield: 38–42 g 
 
 
 Time: 28–32 seconds 
 
 
 Ratio: ~1:2.1 
 
 
 Thick chocolate body, structured fruit sweetness, long clean finish. 
 
 Details 
 
 
 Origin: Uganda 
 
 
 Process: Carbonic Maceration 
 
 
 Roast: Medium Omni 
 
 
 Brew For: Filter & Espresso 
 
 
 Fermented in control. Roasted for clarity. Built for depth

Tasting_Notes: Fruity • Jammy • Wild Ratnagiri Natural Cut is where things get interesting
Desc:
Fruity • Jammy • Wild  
 Ratnagiri Natural Cut is where things get interesting. 
 This is coffee pushed to its expressive edge—bold fruit notes, fermented sweetness, and a heavier body that lingers long after the last sip. It’s not subtle, and it’s not trying to be. 
 Expect bursts of juicy red fruits, syrupy sweetness, and a slightly wild finish that makes every cup feel alive. This is the kind of coffee that stands out instantly—loud, complex, and unapologetically different. 
 Not for everyone. But unforgettable for the right palate. 
 
 What to Expect 
 
 Juicy, fruit-forward profile 
 Jammy sweetness with depth 
 Heavy body with lingering finish 
 Slightly funky, experimental character 
 
 
  Details 
 
 
 Origin:  Ratnagiri Estate, India 
 
 Process:  Natural 
 
 Varietal:  SLN 9 
 
 Roast Level:  Medium 
 
 Best For:  Pour Over, Aeropress, Espresso (for adventurous shots) 
 
 
 Why You’ll Love It 
 If you enjoy coffees that push boundaries and surprise you every sip—this is exactly that.

 This is the kind of coffee you reach for daily but it never feels ordinary.

 Clean, cocoa-led profile 
 Balanced sweetness with mild brightness 
 Smooth, structured finish 
 Easy to dial in across brew methods 
 
 
 Details 
 
 
 Origin:  Ratnagiri Estate, India 
 
 Process:  Washed 
 
 Varietal:  SLN 9 
 
 Roast Level:  Medium 
 
 Best For:  Espresso, Pour Over, French Press 
 
 
 Why You’ll Love It

Name: ANAEROBIC NATURALS- AMMIKULAVI ESTATE
Tasting_Notes: PLUM CAKE, LEMON VERBENA, SPICE, STRAWBERRY, CACAO NIBS Best Brewed with: POUR-OVER
Desc:
FROM THE COOL, ELEVATED LANDSCAPE OF THE PULNEY HILLS IN TAMIL NADU COMES A COFFEE SHAPED BY CAREFUL HANDWORK, CONTROLLED FERMENTATION, AND TIME. THIS IS OUR FIRST COLLABORATION WITH THE AMMIKULAVI ESTATE, LOCATED NEAR KODAIKANAL AT AROUND 1400 MASL, WHERE SLOW CHERRY DEVELOPMENT AND COOL CLIMATES ALLOW FLAVOUR TO FORM WITH DEPTH AND STRUCTURE. 
 THIS MICROL0T IS PRODUCED USING A 72-HOUR ANAEROBIC FERMENTATION, WHERE RIPE, HAND-PICKED CHERRIES ARE SEALED IN AIRTIGHT BARRELS TO DEVELOP SWEETNESS AND COMPLEXITY IN A CONTROLLED, OXYGEN-FREE ENVIRONMENT. FOLLOWING FERMENTATION, THE COFFEE IS WASHED, BRIEFLY SUN-DRIED, AND THEN SHADE-DRIED SLOWLY ON RAISED BEDS. A FINAL RESTING PERIOD ALLOWS THE FLAVOURS TO STABILISE AND INTEGRATE FULLY. 
 IN THE CUP, THIS COFFEE IS LAYERED AND EXPRESSIVE, WITH NOTES OF PLUM CAKE, LEMON VERBENA, WARM SPICE, STRAWBERRY, AND CACAO NIBS. ROASTED MEDIUM-LIGHT, IT MAINTAINS CLARITY AND SWEETNESS WHILE OFFERING A ROUNDED BODY AND STRUCTURED FINISH. 
 THIS IS A COFFEE THAT REFLECTS ITS PROCESS AND PLACE HONESTLY — PATIENT, BALANCED, AND QUIETLY COMPLEX.

Name: Tricolate Coffee Brewer
Desc:
The Right Conditions for High Extractions 
 Taking inspiration from precision pouring accessories and flat-bed brewers alike, the Tricolate offers more control over flow rate, agitation, and percolation than most brewers and significantly reduces the possibility of channeling. This is achieved by a combination of elements, including the flat bottom and its form-fitting filter, which eliminate bypass, ensuring that all the liquid in the cup after the brew will contain coffee solids; the wide base (80mm in diameter) and vertical walls, which make for a shallow, even coffee bed that creates the ideal conditions for uniform water-coffee contact; and the dispersion screen, which distributes the water evenly, reducing the likelihood of channeling. The result of such a finely tuned brewing system is high extraction, which translates to the palate as dense flavor. 
 Agitation With Minimal Effort 
 An oft-overlooked aspect of pour-over brewing is the pour itself, which has the dual responsibility of evenly saturating and satisfactorily agitating the coffee grounds with the water. Although this sounds easy, it is not, and is most often helped along by a special gooseneck kettle and a steady hand. Tricolate, however, has removed that one variable from the equation. The precision holes in the Tricolate's dispersion screen control the flow rate, dictating how much water can get through at any given time, and the screen itself, mounted roughly four inches above the base, controls the pour height and therefore the agitation. As a result, it is possible to achieve consistently high extractions with minimal effort and with any kettle. All that is required for a perfect brew is the appropriate grind size and water temperature. The Tricolate will do the rest. 
 Environmentally Sound 
 The Tricolate is made in Australia of Tritan plastic, which is durable, heat-stable, and free from BPA, BPS, or other bisphenols. The German-made filters, a bag of which is included in the package, have a consistent pore structure, another reason for the high extractions, and, being relatively small, are made from less paper than those for traditional pour over brewers, reducing the environmental impact of every brew.

Name: Intenso Fermentation
Tasting_Notes: candied fruits and berries in the cup with a prominent acidity and complexity
Desc:
This nano-lot from Baarbara Estate was produced by adding yeast to the ripened cherries in a controlled environment. The fermentation process results in notes of candied fruits and berries in the cup with a prominent acidity and complexity.   
  This is the first year we experiment with yeast fermentation. For this lot, we chose a yeast called Intenso (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), intended to increase fruity flavours, mouthfeel and general cup quality.   
  We found a floral aroma and notes of pomegranate, cherry, candied fruit and a hints of prunes supported by a smooth mouthfeel and the best way to enjoy this is to either brew a pour over or an iced coffee.   
  We have cupped this coffee multiple times in different stages of harvest and roast profiles. It can be strange and puzzling (in a nice way) because the flavours are constantly developing. It's like watching your favourite movie, that you've forgotten.

Tasting_Notes: pineapple, honey, sweet lime, and tangerine; offering both brightness and balance in the cup
Desc:

The process is closely monitored for pH and temperature to ensure consistency, with a 1:2 coffee-to-fruit ratio enhancing complexity. Our favourite lot this year - we also like to call it a Fruit Punch!

Name: Couverture Canephora - Roasted on 29/03
Tasting_Notes: Chocolatey, berry-like, boozy, all in the same coffee?
Desc:
Fine Cup Award Winning Process  
 Exclusive Lot. Limited Edition: 16 kgs. 
 Chocolatey, berry-like, boozy, all in the same coffee? Yes, the complexity of this coffee is truly mind boggling! 
  This is the 3rd year of us bringing the Couverture Canephora to you. This beautiful Robusta is grown by Mr Mahesh Nayananan of TheNaturalFarmer, based in Pulneys, Tamil Nadu, and fermented using their proprietary methods.  
 Canephora, an old name of the Robusta, has us coming back for more. This coffee is fruity, acidic, and chocolatey - with zero bitterness, all at the same time! Tasting this coffee is like drinking a light and boozy Madagascar hot chocolate. Isn’t that mind-blowing? This coffee is a  limited lot of 16kg , and has won the Flavour of India - Fine Cup Award 2023 for Robusta Naturals. 
 We cupped the first edition of this coffee blind, with 5 people, and none of them could say it was a Robusta. It continues to blow many more minds ever since. 
 The coffee beans that go into Couverture Canephora were nurtured for 17 months - 12 months on the plant, 15 days for fermentation, and 4.5 months, for extended slow drying. The result of so much time, love, effort, and attention is something so complex, it opened our eyes.  Coming from sir Mahesh Narayanan and the team at TheNaturalFarmer, this coffee clearly reflects the excellent cultivation practices that the coffee has received during the harvest and beyond, from the nurturing of sapling to plant.

Name: Kora Zinfandel - Roasted on 05/05
Tasting_Notes: We have a new daily favourite for the pour-over lovers in the house At the cupping table
Process: it themselves, on their land, with their hands
Desc:
We have a new daily favourite for the pour-over lovers in the house 
 At the cupping table, we expected what a well-processed washed coffee typically delivers: clean, chcoolatey, nutty, classic. What we got instead was a cup so fruit-forward it made us double-check the coffee. It's washed, and Ajay, the Q grader, verified this in his cupping notes. 
 This coffee comes from the members of Duduma Farmers Producer Company, rooted in the Lamtaput and Nandapur blocks of Koraput district, Odisha. A community of 841 farmer members — 561 of them coffee growers — 80% from Scheduled Tribes communities,  over 62% women . They don't just grow this coffee. They process it themselves, on their land, with their hands. 
 With the intention to keep the value in the hands of the growers, we don't buy cherries. We source only what the community grows and processes — and when the quality meets specialty grade, we pay accordingly. This harvest earned a 15–20% premium over prevailing market prices. The cup earned it. 
 We roasted this to a medium profile to let the fruitiness come forward cleanly. The result is a cup with gentle acidity, warmth, and just enough complexity to keep you interested — morning or evening, pour-over, Aeropress or even a fruity cold brew. 
  A washed coffee that forgot the rules. Our favourite kind.  
   
 
 
 
  Taste Profile 
 
  
 
 Citrus, Chocolate, Slightly Fruity, Plum like, Nutty  
 
 
 
 
 Origin 
 
    Lamtaput, Koraput, Odisha  
 
 
 
 Processing 
 
  
 Traditional Washed 
 
 
 
 Elevation 
 
     3000+ ft

Name: Maison Mahua - Roasted on 27/03
Desc:
Limited Lot of 30kg only.   In the hills of Punjisil village, on the banks of the  Punjisil Falls , a community of 50 families nurtures this 75 acres of land - 1.5 acres awarded to each beneficiary - an eligible member of the family, harvesting coffee that grows wild among forest cover and stream-fed slopes — where access requires a long, steep walk from the village, and crossing the river stream on foot. 
 Here, harvesting remains a community act, guided by rhythm rather than machinery. Ripe red cherries are hand-carried for over two kilometres, across the river, where they’re de-pulped by a hand-operated pulper, then naturally fermented overnight in the cool, running water of the stream itself. The coffee is then sun-dried on handmade wooden beds, built from locally and seasonally available timber and leaves. Each farmer keeps their parchment at home until moisture is checked and lots are aggregated. 
 Roasted to a medium profile that is suitable for both espresso as well as filter, the resulting cup has a body we fell in love with. It's the kind of cup that you can have everyday, whether as a morning cheer me up, or as a quite wind down at the end of day.

     Roasted Nuts, Milk Chocolate, Citrus Zest, Vanilla

 Traditional Washed

     3000+ ft

Name: Prosecco Aventi - Roasted on 19/04
Tasting_Notes: As it cools, a sweet pickled lemon brightness lifts through, tart but rounded
Desc:
Taste Profile  - Winy, Sweet Pickled Lemon, Malt 
 
 
 
 Origin  -   Koraput A1 Coffee Estate, Koraput, Odisha 
 
 
 
 Varietal -  Catimor 
 
 
 
 Processing  - Extended Anaerobic Honey, 240 hrs sun-dried, Split beans 
 
 
 
 Elevation  - 3200 ft 
 
 
 
   
  Roast:  Medium  Acidity:  Bright  Sweetness:  High 
 From award-winning estate - Koraput A1 Estate 
 Limited edition of 10kg only 
  During harvest, unseasonal rainfall caused a portion of cherries to split — raising the very real risk of farmer losses. Rather than discard them, the lot was carefully segregated and given a second chance through one of the most labour-intensive processes in specialty coffee.   
 Each cherry was manually sorted, floated to remove defects, and sealed into fermentation vessels under oxygen-limited conditions for a full 240 hours — 10 days of controlled anaerobic fermentation, closely monitored to build aromatic complexity without tipping into over-fermentation.       
 Post-fermentation, the cherries were depulped with generous mucilage retained — the honey process — and moved to raised drying beds. Given the compromised skins, drying was managed with frequent turning to ensure even moisture migration. The parchment was then conditioned, rested, and dry-milled to grade.        
 Ten days of patience show up exactly where they should. The cup opens with a    winy depth    — that unmistakable ferment character that lingers on the sides of your tongue. As it cools, a    sweet pickled lemon    brightness lifts through, tart but rounded, like a preserved citrus rather than a sharp acid. The finish is long and grounding —    malt    warmth that settles everything into place. Best brewed slow. Best drunk without distraction.

Name: Robustas of Coorg - Roasted on 02/04
Tasting_Notes: chocolates, prunes, and raisins
Origin: estates with less than a ton of production
Desc:
India is a land of smallholder farmers - and even coffee is grown at estates with less than a ton of production. And do you know what is the smallest quantity that can be graded and sorted in most affordable curing houses? A ton. So while we like the highest grade and best bean density in our coffee, the smallholders who do good work, don't get the limelight that they should, for the hard work they put in. Robusta is a healthy child that has adapted well to climate change, and is soon turning into the highlight of this industry, Worldwide.    
  Bhavika states that she had her biases against robusta - but this is the  first coffee  ever, that opened her mind to the possibilities that robusta holds in its folds. She believes it could be the first robusta for a lot of people, too!  
  The roasting, if Robusta conscious (credits to Rajeev Vaishnav), the sweetness and complexity in the bean can develop and shine. Bringing to you, a washed Robusta that is sensitive to the Indian small-holders, a roast that bears in mind the qualities of the bean, and brings you, nothing but the best. The coffee will remind you of chocolates, prunes, and raisins.  
  Proudly presenting, Robustas of Coorg.  
  Special thanks to Ujjwal Rathi for ensuring that his love for this coffee and consistent reminders made us stay on track to share this coffee with the rest of the fam.  
  Recommended Brewing Temperature: 85 Degrees Celcius

Name: Trousseau Adwaita - Roasted on 22/04
Tasting_Notes: Strawberry and apple bring brightness upfront
Desc:
Many coffees promise a great cup. This one has already proven it. 
 Lot A20L13 from Koraput A1 Coffee Estate is a two-time winner of the Flavour of India – Fine Cup Award (2023 & 2024) — not by accident, but by design. Every detail, from harvest to cup, is deliberate. 
 Grown at 3,200 feet in the hills of Koraput, Odisha, the Chandragiri variety here is handled with the kind of care that turns great fruit into something memorable. Ripe cherries are hand-sorted, depulped, and sealed into fermentation tanks for exactly 48 hours. Inside, pH and temperature are tracked closely — controlled microbial activity, balanced sugar breakdown, and layered flavor development without the risk of over-fermentation. 
 What emerges from the tank goes straight to raised drying beds, coated in a rich layer of honey-process mucilage. Sun-dried slowly, turned regularly, and rested before dry milling — this is patience built into every step. 
 In the cup, that patience shows. Strawberry and apple bring brightness upfront. Almond and caramel deepen the mid-palate. A long, sweet finish ties it all together — clean, complex, and unmistakably Chandragiri. 
 Expect this coffee to open up 3 weeks post roast, subject to altitude and local climatic conditions.  
  Recognition:    Flavour of India – Fine Cup Award 2023 & 2024 
 
 
 
 
 Taste Profile  - Strawberry, Almond, Caramel, Apple, Sweet Finish 
 
 
 
 Origin  -   Koraput A1 Coffee Estate, Koraput, Odisha 
 
 
 
 Varietal -  Chandragiri 
 
 
 
 Processing  - 36 hrs Anaerobic Honey Sundried  
 
 
 
 Elevation  - 3200 ft 
 
 
 
   
  Roast:  Light to Medium  Acidity:  Bright  Sweetness:  High 
   Limited edition of 70kg only

Desc:
Nestled within the vast scape of the Western Ghats   in India, is the Malnad region of Karnataka, with its rich   heritage, culture and abundance of some   of India’s best coffee plantations. Situated in   Sakleshpur in the historic Munjarabad region, lies   HARLEY ESTATE dating back to the early 1860’s.   The plantation consists of crops such as Coffee,   Pepper, Cardamom, Cocoa, Bananas, Areca, Vanilla and Coconut. All crops are carefully planted in   between natural and jungle shade tress.

The result is vibrant cup with layered complexity, delicate citrus nuances, and a refined aromatic finish.

Name: Champagne Naturals
Tasting_Notes: During fermentation, we use yeast in the purpose-built room, carefully monitoring the pH and temperature for several
Desc:
Once the ripe cherries are handpicked by our team, we triple wash the fruits to remove any floaters and defective beans from the lot. We specifically choose cherries with a Brix value of 25 and above to maximize the sugar content in the fruit before fermentation begins. During fermentation, we use yeast in the purpose-built room, carefully monitoring the pH and temperature for several hours to create a fruity and complex cup. Once fermentation is complete, we sun-dry the cherries on raised beds for 30 days and allow them to rest for 4 weeks before shipment.

Desc:

Name: The Lacto Project
Tasting_Notes: [Meta Description]: Discover Coffeeverse The Lacto Project – a 100% Arabica specialty coffee crafted with cherry
Desc:
This coffee has undergone a 96-hour extended carbonic maceration. Processed naturally, made from the Hemavathi varietal, grown at 4500 feet in the SIVERMARA Patte block. The cherries had a Brix of 25.9 at harvest and were placed in Bio fermenters after floater removal. They were inoculated with various lab-grown cultures, purged with carbon dioxide, and fermented for 96 hours. After fermentation, the beans were dried slowly on raised beds for 31 days, with constant stirring.
[Meta Description]: Discover Coffeeverse The Lacto Project – a 100% Arabica specialty coffee crafted with cherry processing for a clean, balanced cup and gentle natural sweetness.

Desc:
Tastes Like  -   Green Apple, Muskmelon and Rounded mouthfeel 
 
 Roasting Profile     -   Espresso profile (Medium Roast) 
 
 
 Process     -    Washed  
 
   Varietal -  S 795  
   Altitude -  1470  MASL    
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Thouqeer Ahamed   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
    Coffee Producers Note  -    At our estate, every coffee bean carries the story of a season shaped by nature, care, and tradition. Coffee cultivation is not just farming for us-it is a craft passed down through generations. From the first rains that awaken the blossoms to the final drying of cherries under the sun, each step is guided with patience and precision.  
     Roasters Note  -     This lot was developed for espresso to bring out its crisp green apple acidity and subtle muskmelon sweetness, while maintaining a rounded and balanced mouthfeel. The roast profile was tuned to preserve clarity and fruit expression without compromising body, making it versatile both as a straight shot and in milk-based beverages.

Name: Melkodige Estate Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals
Tasting_Notes: Pomegranate, Pink Guava and Golden Raisins
Desc:
Tastes Like  -   Pomegranate, Pink Guava and Golden Raisins 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals 
 
   Varietal -  Sl 9  
   Altitude -  1280 MASL    
   Producer Name     -  Aveen and Yogita Rodrigues   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -       R  ed, fully ripe cherries with a Brix level above 22 are selectively handpicked and carefully cleaned using a water bath to remove impurities and lighter fruit. The cherries then undergo anaerobic fermentation in sealed drums for 72 hours, allowing complex flavours to develop. 
 Post-fermentation, they are transferred to raised wooden drying beds and dried slowly under shade nets. During this stage, the cherries are regularly raked to ensure even and consistent drying. Once fully dried, they are packed into gunny bags and rested for 60 days, allowing the flavours to stabilise and mature before further processing. 
      Roasters Note  -      We’ve taken this coffee light to preserve its vibrancy and showcase the fruit character developed during fermentation. Expect a bright, expressive cup with juicy acidity and a clean, lingering sweetness. In the cup: Pomegranate leads with a fresh, winey brightness, followed by soft pink guava and a rounded golden raisin sweetness on the finish. The body is smooth and supple, with a crisp yet balanced aftertaste. Best enjoyed when brewed clean and slightly cooler to let the fruit open up gradually.

Name: Salawara Estate Bioreactor Naturals
Tasting_Notes: Spiced Mandarin Tea , Dried Apple and Cranberry
Desc:
Tastes Like  -   Spiced Mandarin Tea , Dried Apple and Cranberry  
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Naturals 
 
   Varietal -  SL 795  
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     This lot was fermented in our newly introduced bioreactor, a state-of-the-art fermentation system designed to ensure precise control and homogeneous fermentation. The coffees were placed in the bioreactor for 72 hours, where temperature, oxygen levels, and microbial activity were carefully managed. A specially selected yeast strain was introduced during fermentation to enhance and amplify the fruit-forward characteristics of the coffee. Once fermentation was complete, the coffee was removed from the bioreactor and dried slowly on raised beds, allowing the developed flavors to stabilize and fully express themselves in the final cup.  
      Roasters Note  -       This coffee is a beautiful example of controlled fermentation done right. Processed in a state-of-the-art bioreactor over 72 hours with carefully managed temperature, oxygen, and a selected yeast strain, the result is an exceptionally clean yet expressive cup. Roasted for filter to highlight clarity and sweetness, it opens up with a vibrant spiced mandarin tea character, followed by layers of dried apple and a crisp cranberry finish. Bright, fruit-forward, and structured , a lot that feels both lively and refined.

Desc:
Tastes Like  -    Watermelon, Orange Blossom, and Damson Plum          
 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Carbonic Maceration Naturals  
 
   Varietal -   SL 795 + SL 6   
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     Ripe coffee cherries are carefully handpicked from  Dodda kere Patte, at a Brix level of 24. The cherries are then sealed in stainless steel tanks and pressurized with carbon dioxide for 72 hours, creating an anaerobic environment that initiates carbonic maceration. During this stage, intracellular fermentation occurs within the intact cherries, intensifying fruit-forward characteristics and enhancing aromatic complexity. After fermentation, the cherries are removed from the tanks and slowly dried on raised beds, preserving clarity, sweetness, and vibrant fruity flavors in the cup.  
      Roasters Note  -      We roasted this carbonic maceration lot with a focus on clarity and fruit expression. The profile brings out its watermelon-like juiciness and orange blossom aromatics, supported by a deeper damson plum sweetness. Development was kept controlled to retain acidity and structure while preserving a light, refreshing finish.

Name: SCA Brewing Foundation Course
Process: ing methods, and best practices for coffee storage
Desc:
The Brewing Foundation course offers a comprehensive introduction to the art and science of coffee brewing. Through both theory and hands-on practice, learners are guided through various brewing methods using a range of devices. 
 This course is ideal for beginners and provides the fundamental skills and knowledge needed to craft delicious brewed coffee.  
  Time:  10:30 AM - 6:30 PM 
  Location:  Corridor Seven Coffee Academy [ Map Link ] 
  What You'll Learn:    
  1. Coffee Knowledge :  Understand Arabica vs. Robusta, processing methods, and best practices for coffee storage. 
  2. Brewing Methods & Equipment :  Explore manual brewers like V60, French Press, and AeroPress, and learn how to use essential brewing tools. 
  3. Brewing Guidelines :  Master the 7 key elements of brewing: ratio, grind, time, temperature, turbulence, water quality, and filter type. 
  4. Brewing Techniques :  Practice percolation (V60), immersion (French Press), and hybrid (AeroPress) brewing styles. 
  5. Brew Analysis :  Learn to evaluate your brew by analyzing its color, aroma, taste, and body. 
  6. Equipment Maintenance :  Maintain your brewing tools for consistency, cleanliness, and long-term performance. 
 With a strong focus on practical application, participants will learn how to brew thoughtfully, evaluate their results, and make informed adjustments. The course concludes with a written assessment to test your grasp of the foundational concepts. 
  Who Should Enroll  
 The SCA Brewing Foundation course is designed for: 
 -  Home Brewers  eager to explore the world of coffee at home 
 -  Aspiring Baristas  and individuals interested in building a career in the food and beverage industry 
  Course Outcome  
 Participants who complete both the  practical exam during the course  and the  online written exam  afterward will receive the  SCA Brewing Foundation Certificate , an internationally recognized credential that also contributes toward the SCA Coffee Diploma .  
  Course Fee  
 INR 23,600 (inclusive of GST) 
  Fee Included  
 - Access to the globally respected SCA coffee education system 
 - Comprehensive course materials and reference notes 
 - Certification upon successful completion of all assessments and exams. 
  Certification:  
 Upon successful completion of both the practical and theoretical exams, participants will receive the  SCA Brewing Foundation Certificate.  
  About the Trainer  
  Naitik Shah  grew up in Muscat, Oman, where an early exposure to café culture sparked his passion for coffee. He now leads the coffee program at  Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters  and is a certified  SCA Authorized Trainer (AST)  in Brewing. 
 With hands-on experience across brewing, sensory analysis, and the broader coffee value chain, Naitik also brings a trained eye as a  judge at national-level latte art competitions . His teaching blends global standards with real-world insights—perfect for anyone looking to build a solid foundation in specialty coffee. 
  Why Join Us?  
 - Small batch classes for focused learning 
 - Access to professional cupping and brewing equipment 
 - A supportive space to ask questions, taste widely, and grow confidently in coffee knowledge 
 - Part of the broader Coffee Skills Program that includes advanced modules in Brewing, and more 
 Start your journey into specialty coffee with clarity, confidence, and curiosity. 
  For bookings or more information, contact:  [impact@corridorseven.coffee](mailto:impact@corridorseven.coffee) or 9767750960

Name: SCA Brewing Intermediate Course
Desc:
Take the next step in your coffee journey with the SCA Brewing Intermediate course at Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters. This intensive 2-day course is designed for experienced brewers and coffee enthusiasts ready to master their craft and earn an internationally recognized certification.  
  Perfect for anyone who has completed the Foundation course, this program goes beyond the basics to deepen your understanding of the science and art of brewing. You will gain advanced coffee brewing skills through a mix of theory and hands-on practice, empowering you to consistently produce exceptional coffee.  
   What You'll Learn   
  Our comprehensive coffee brewing course covers essential topics to help you elevate your brews:  
 
 
   Advanced Brewing Principles:  Learn the key variables that influence brew strength and coffee extraction for ultimate cup quality.  
 
 
   Sensory Analysis:  Develop your coffee sensory skills to evaluate brews, assessing aroma, taste, body, and flavor with confidence.  
 
 
   Controlling Variables:  Master the impact of grind size, brewing time, water temperature, and turbulence on your coffee.  
 
 
   Expert Techniques:  Identify and correct common issues like under, over, and uneven extraction.  
 
 
   Roast Level & Water Chemistry:  Understand the effect of roast level and the crucial role of water chemistry on flavor.  
 
 
   Professional Tools:  Get hands-on with tools used to measure soluble concentration and calculate extraction yield.

  This course is led by Naitik Shah, a certified SCA Authorized Trainer (AST) and the head of the coffee program at Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters. Naitik brings a wealth of hands-on experience in brewing, sensory analysis, and the broader specialty coffee industry. His expertise ensures you receive a solid foundation that blends global standards with real-world insights, preparing you for the SCA Coffee Courses.  
   Course Details & Outcomes   
  Upon successful completion of the in-person practical exam and the online written exam, you will receive your official SCA Brewing Intermediate Certificate. This credential is an industry standard for professional brewers and a significant step in your coffee education journey.

  Your course fee includes access to all comprehensive materials, professional brewing equipment, and your SCA certificate upon successful completion.

Name: SCA Brewing Professional Course
Desc:
The  SCA Brewing Professional  course is where science meets mastery. Designed for those who have completed the SCA  Brewing Intermediate  level, this advanced program takes you deep into the chemistry, physics, and sensory dimensions of coffee brewing. Over 21 hours (3 days) of focused learning, you’ll sharpen your analytical skills, refine your brewing precision, and earn an internationally recognized certification that sets you apart in the world of specialty coffee. 
 This course isn’t just about brewing, it’s about thinking like a brewer. You’ll learn to measure, evaluate, and manipulate key variables to achieve consistent, exceptional results across different brewing devices and conditions. Whether you’re managing a café, consulting for clients, or simply pushing the limits of your craft, this program equips you with the mindset and tools to lead in the field. 
 
 
  Delivery:  In-person 
 
 
  Prerequisites:  
 
 
  Required:  SCA Brewing Intermediate 
 
 
 
 
  Exams:  Written and Practical  
 
 
  Date:   21  st   - 22  nd   - 23r d  April 2026  
 
 
  Time:  10:00 AM – 7:30 PM  (including breaks) (3 days)  
 
 
  Course Fee:  INR 53,100 (inclusive of GST) 
 
 
 Your course fee covers all professional brewing equipment, study materials, and access to your SCA certification exams. 
 Upon successful completion, you’ll receive the  SCA Brewing Professional Certificate , recognized globally as the standard for professional coffee brewers. 
  What You’ll Learn  
 The Brewing Professional course builds on prior knowledge and takes you into the heart of brewing science: 
  1. Advanced Coffee Knowledge  Understand how roast level influences extraction, flavor, and sensory perception. 
  2. Brewing Methods & Equipment  Explore how device shapes, bed depth, and filter media affect brewing outcomes. Learn how to select, calibrate, and optimize gravity brewers for precision brewing. 
  3. Brewing Guidelines  Dive into the  7 Essential Elements of Brewing  and master the relationships between grind size, particle distribution, brewing time, temperature, and turbulence. 
  4. Water Chemistry & Quality  Gain an expert understanding of water’s origin, hardness, alkalinity, and treatment methods. Learn to test and modify water composition to bring out the best in your coffee. 
  5. Brewing Process  Analyze each brewing phase from wetting and blooming to extraction and yield calculation while understanding how these affect sensory results. 
  6. Brew Analysis & Sensory Evaluation  Measure soluble yield and concentration, describe a balanced brew, and use professional tools to interpret data and sensory feedback accurately. 
  7. Maintenance & Optimization  Learn how grinder burr quality and replacement cycles affect consistency, and explore the sensory and technical impact of bypass brewing techniques. 
  About Your Certified SCA Trainer  
 This course is led by  Naitik Shah , a certified SCA Authorized Trainer (AST) and head of the coffee program at  Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters . With years of hands-on experience in brewing and sensory development, Naitik brings a unique blend of technical expertise and real-world coffee insight. His approach emphasizes clarity, curiosity, and mastery helping you connect science with practice in meaningful ways. 
 For bookings and more information:  Email:   impact@corridorseven.coffee        Phone:  9767750960

Name: ARABICA PEABERRY COFFEE
Tasting_Notes: At Devans, Arabica Peaberry is
Desc:
ANIMAL PRINTED PACKS AVAILABLE IN 500 g ONLY 
  Indian coffees are home to the best shade grown coffees in the world. It grows Arabica and Robusta coffees in the southern states where lush coffee plantations are heavily inter cropped with black pepper and ginger that bustle with honeybees and yield the finest coffee beans.  
  Peaberry coffees are rare, comprising only 3-7% of the total crop. These pea-shaped, natural formations of the coffee bean are thought to form when several pistils get knocked off the coffee flower, causing only one seed to form inside the coffee fruit rather than two.  
  Normally coffee beans grow two to a cherry, flat against each other but in about five percent of the worlds coffee a bean is found to be solo that's Peaberry.  
  Because there's no way to tell from looking at the cherry whether there's a single or double bean inside, as a result Peaberry beans are hand picked and processed to be enjoyed separately.  
 Tasting notes:    
  At Devans, Arabica Peaberry is roasted in a way to create a mild strength of coffee, that is soft, smooth, highly aromatic and flavorful . If you like milder coffees, go for this lighter bodied and a clean cup of coffee. It’s ideal when made in a French Press or a pour over.

Name: CRIMSON SPIRIT - Pineapple Ferment - Kalyancool Estate (In-House)
Tasting_Notes: 🍍 Pineapple Candy 🍈 Jackfruit 🥭 Mango 🍓 Strawberry 🍑 Plum 🥃 Whiskey-like Booziness Experience Kalyancool Pineapple
Desc:
Kalyancool Pineapple Fermentation – Crimson Spirit   
 This is the best microlot we have roasted in last 365 days.. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:   Light Plus  
  100% Arabica   
 Rooted in our own estate at Kalyancool, this experimental microlot celebrates precision fermentation and fruit-forward innovation. Crafted from  350 kg of fully ripened red cherries , this lot undergoes an  anaerobic natural fermentation  enhanced with  75 kg of fresh pineapple , carefully integrated with a  developed yeast strain  to guide flavor clarity and intensity. 
 Fermented for  72 hours  with the fruit intact, this process unlocks a bold tropical expression while preserving balance and structure. The cup opens with an unmistakable  pineapple candy sweetness , juicy and playful, followed by layers of  jackfruit and ripe mango richness . As it cools, elegant hints of  strawberry and plum  emerge, finishing with a  whiskey-like boozy warmth  that lingers beautifully. 
 This is a confident, expressive coffee—crafted to stand out, not blend in.

 Varietal: Chandragiri, Selection 795

Name: CT Estate – Caramelized Lychee (Yellow Honey Process)
Tasting_Notes: 🍵 Floral Tea 🍇 Mulberry 🍯 Honey Sugar 🍈 Lychee Experience the delicate sophistication of Caramelized Lychee
Desc:
CT Estate – Caramelized Lychee (Yellow Honey Process)   
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
 Nestled in the rich coffee-growing belt of Chikmagalur,  CT Estate , under the careful stewardship of  Mr. Sufyan , presents  Caramelized Lychee —a refined and expressive microlot crafted with a strong focus on quality and precision. Known for his meticulous approach to cultivation and processing, Sufyan has been consistently producing clean, character-driven coffees that highlight both terroir and innovation. 
 This lot undergoes a carefully controlled  Yellow Honey process , where a portion of the mucilage is retained during drying to enhance sweetness and clarity. The result is a beautifully clean yet layered cup, where delicate florals meet fruit-forward brightness. 
 In the cup, expect a graceful and aromatic profile led by  floral tea-like notes , complemented by the soft juiciness of  mulberry  and the smooth sweetness of  honeyed sugar . A gentle  lychee brightness  ties the profile together, creating a cup that is both elegant and refreshing. 
 📍  CT Estate – Chikmagalur, Karnataka  🌿  Varietals:  Chandragiri & 5B | Elevation: 3600–3900 ft 🕒  Yellow Honey Process  🌞  Carefully Shade-Dried for Optimal Sweetness  
 
   Tasting Notes:   
 🍵 Floral Tea 🍇 Mulberry 🍯 Honey Sugar 🍈 Lychee 
 
 Experience the delicate sophistication of  Caramelized Lychee , where floral clarity and fruit sweetness come together in a light, refined, and highly drinkable cup.

Name: Frozen Cherry Imperial - Jannapura Estate
Tasting_Notes: 🍒 Cherry-forward sweetness 🍵 Earl Grey tea elegance 🥤 Cola-like depth 🍎 Apple brightness 🍇 Dry berries & raisin
Desc:
Jannapura Estate – Frozen Cherry Imperial  
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
 Perched in the lush highlands of Chikmagalur, Jannapura Estate presents  Frozen Cherry Imperial —a bold and experimental nanolot that redefines fruit-forward coffee through precision processing and controlled fermentation. 
 This lot begins with carefully handpicked, fully ripened coffee cherries that are  frozen in an industrial freezer for 48 hours . This freezing step enhances cellular breakdown, allowing deeper infusion of flavours during the next stage. The cherries are then  anaerobically fermented with yeast , developing a complex and layered profile, before being  slowly dried on raised beds for 18 days  to lock in clarity and sweetness. 
 The result is a strikingly expressive cup—vivid, structured, and deeply aromatic. Expect a unique interplay of tea-like elegance and dark fruit intensity, with a profile that stands apart in both complexity and character. 
 📍  Jannapura Estate – Chikmagalur, Karnataka  🌿  Varietals:  Selection 795 | Elevation: 3600–3900 ft 🕒  48h Cryo (Frozen) + Anaerobic Fermentation  🌞  18 Days Raised Bed Drying  
 
  Tasting Notes:  
 🍒 Cherry-forward sweetness 🍵 Earl Grey tea elegance 🥤 Cola-like depth 🍎 Apple brightness 🍇 Dry berries & raisin richness 
 
 Experience the intensity of  Frozen Cherry Imperial , where controlled freezing meets fermentation to create a cup that is both innovative and unmistakably premium. 
  Resting Period = Minimum 10 days.

 Sourced from a  single lot at Ratnagiri Estate , this coffee is crafted from carefully harvested ripe cherries with a  Brix level of 23.8 , indicating excellent fruit maturity and sugar development. 
 The cherries come from  Block 5/1 of the 17 Acres Patte section , planted with the  Catuai varietal , known for its clean structure and ability to express terroir-driven sweetness.

This is followed by subtle layers of  mulberry, grapes, and guava , adding gentle fruit complexity. As the coffee cools, softer notes of  banana and delicate black tea  appear, bringing a refined, elegant finish with a lingering sweetness. 
 This is a terroir-focused coffee that highlights how  native microbial fermentation and slow natural drying can produce a clean yet deeply sweet cup.

Desc:
Kalyancool Thermal Shock Fermentation – Ruby Pulse  
 This is one of the most technically experimental microlots we have produced this year—an expressive coffee that demonstrates how extreme temperature contrast and controlled fermentation can unlock deep fruit complexity and wine-like character. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
  100% Arabica  
 Rooted in our own estate at  Kalyancool , this microlot explores the effect of  thermal shock processing combined with controlled yeast fermentation . Carefully selected fully ripened red cherries are first sorted to remove floaters and underripe fruits, ensuring only dense, high-quality cherries enter the process. 
 The cherries are then subjected to a  thermal shock treatment , where they are immersed in  55°C warm water for 5 minutes . This controlled heat exposure helps soften the fruit structure and prepares the cherries for rapid cellular stress. Immediately after heating, the cherries are transferred to  ice chamber and rapidly chilled , remaining in the cold bath for around  7–8 minutes . 
 This dramatic temperature contrast creates a “thermal shock” effect that enhances permeability of the fruit and intensifies the interaction between sugars, microbes, and yeast during fermentation. 
 After the thermal treatment, the cherries are gently  bruised to create a bruised natural process , allowing partial opening of the fruit skin while maintaining the natural mucilage and pulp around the beans. 
 The cherries are then inoculated with  activated Lalcafe Intenso yeast , a strain chosen for its ability to enhance fruity aromatics and wine-like complexity. Fermentation takes place in  sealed Eco-tact bags for 72 hours , allowing controlled anaerobic conditions to develop layered fruit character. 
 Once fermentation is complete, the coffee is dried as naturals and carefully  light (light plus) roasted  to preserve clarity, acidity, and aromatic intensity. 
 The cup opens with  fresh watermelon sweetness , juicy and refreshing. This is followed by vibrant  pomegranate acidity , adding brightness and structure. As the coffee develops on the palate, deeper  grape-wine notes emerge , bringing a rich fermented fruit character. As the cup cools, darker fruit layers of  prunes and dried grapes  appear, creating a long, wine-like finish with lingering sweetness. 
 This is a bold experimental coffee designed to showcase how  thermal shock processing and precision fermentation can transform natural coffees into intensely fruit-driven microlots.

  Varietal:  Chandragiri, Selection 795

 🍉 Watermelon 🍷 Grape Wine 🍎 Pomegranate 🍇 Dried Grapes 🍑 Prunes

 Carefully selected ripe cherries are processed as naturals and dried to the ideal moisture level. Once stabilized, the green beans are transferred into  seasoned whisky barrels  that previously held aged whisky. The beans are then  rested inside the barrels for several weeks , allowing the porous green coffee to slowly absorb the aromatic compounds embedded in the oak. 
 During this maturation period, the beans take on subtle layers of  oak wood tannins, vanilla sweetness, and whisky-like aromatic complexity , while still preserving the natural fruit character of the coffee. 
 Once the desired infusion is achieved, the beans are removed and roasted  Light Plus , ensuring the barrel characteristics remain elegant and integrated rather than overpowering.

This is followed by juicy layers of  kiwi, grapes, and stone fruits , adding a lively fruit sweetness that balances the barrel influence. As the coffee develops, the profile deepens into rich  whisky-like warmth , supported by pronounced  oakwood structure  and delicate  vanilla undertones  that linger into the finish.

    Roaster thoughts :      
 We approached the roast with  elevated initial energy and restrained airflow , allowing the coffee to move cleanly through drying while avoiding excessive convection that can flatten aromatics. The profile was kept deliberately short, finishing at an  ultra-light endpoint with 15-16% development , just enough to stabilise the structure without muting the fruit.Anaerobic coffees can easily tip into heavy, ferment-driven profiles. Here, we aimed for the opposite, keeping the cup  transparent and articulate , where fermentation supports rather than dominates. In the cup, this results in a  bright citrus-forward expression , with  orange and green grape acidity , layered with  red apple sweetness , and a softer  fig-like finish  that carries through the aftertaste. The body remains  medium-heavy but clean , with a lifted aromatic profile. 
   Brewing   Note:      Due   to   its   delicate   roast   level,   we   recommend   brewing   this   coffee   with    higher   water   temperatures (97-98°  C)      and   a   controlled   pour   to   ensure   full   extraction.   Attention   to    grind   size,   agitation,   and   brew   time      is   critical   to   achieve   optimal   clarity   and   balance   in   the   cup.  
  This   coffee   is   a   testament   to   our   commitment   to   innovation   and   continuous   refinement   in   roasting.   
 
  Brew Better: Water & Resting Guidelines  
   Dose:   18g   Water:   270g (1:15 ratio)   Temperature:   97–98°C   Grind:   Medium (slightly finer than your standard V60)   Brew Time:   2:30 – 2:50  
 For  more citrus brightness  → go coarser + faster drawdown 
 For  more sweetness & body  → go finer + extend brew to ~3:00 
 Water is just as important as the beans. For the cleanest, most balanced cup, we recommend using **mineral water with a Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) level not above 140 ppm**. This will allow the true flavor of your coffee to shine. 
 Rested Coffee = Better Coffee 
 Freshly roasted coffee continues to evolve. Harsh or roasty notes fade, giving way to sweetness, clarity, and complexity. 
 Our resting guide: 
 Minimum rest (Filter): 10 days after roast date Minimum rest (Espresso): Up to 3 weeks after roast date 
 Patience pays off. Let your coffee settle, and enjoy a cup that truly reflects its origin.

Desc:
Call this sampler pack your ‘First Date’ with coffee with no awkward silences, just three cups ready to sweep you off your feet.   
  Raincheck is the smooth talker, the one with dark chocolate eyes and caramel laughs, the kind that warms you from the inside out.

  All your moods, all your firsts, in one perfect pack.  
  3 pouches of 100gm each

Name: Golden Hour
Tasting_Notes: that one rare moment you actually pause - mid-scroll, mid-chaos - when the sunlight spills in and for no reason at all
Desc:
Like a soft spotlight through the blinds - orange zest, stone fruit, and juicy apple line up for their solo. It's plum, but polished. This cup? It tastes like that one rare moment you actually pause - mid-scroll, mid-chaos - when the sunlight spills in and for no reason at all, you smile. Just for existing. It’s your reminder: reset the clock.  
  ROAST LEVEL:  Medium Light 
   PROCESSING:  Washed 
  REGION:  Hoyasala Estate (  Tamil Nadu ) &  The Laks Farm(Tamil Nadu) 
  ALTITUDE:  1300 MASL (metres above sea level) 
  VARIETAL:  SL9 
  HARVEST:  2025 
  BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual (French Press, Aeropress, Pour-over, Channi style, South Indian Filter) 
  BEVERAGE STYLE:  Manual Brew, Milk Based Drinks  
  Where Golden Hour Grows  Golden Hour is born where stillness meets intention - on two farms that honour the land, the craft, and the quiet magic of doing things the right way. 
 In the Pulney Hills of Tamil Nadu, you’ll find The Laks Farm in Pachalur village. One of the highest coffee-growing regions in India, it's a place where biodiversity thrives, coffee trees growing alongside oranges, bananas, cardamom, and pepper. Everything here is organic, intentional, and deeply alive. The result? Coffees that are bright, layered, and lingering like light catching the edge of the day. 
 Down south in Anoor village, Hoysala Estate carries the weight of history, named after a dynasty that once ruled this very soil. The estate has been family-run since the late 1800s, with a quiet focus on growing coffee that speaks for itself. At 1100 meters, intercropped with cardamom and processed with care - natural, washed, honey, and even monsooned, their approach is steady, patient, and precise. 
 Together, these two farms create something balanced and beautiful. Golden Hour is a blend full of grace and is soft, rounded, and golden in every sense.

Desc:
Ground Rules because coffee isn’t just a drink for some, it’s serious business.

Name: Raincheck
Tasting_Notes: Citrus and sweet lime sneak in like a memory
Desc:
Heavy-bodied and emotionally available. Caramel wraps you like an old jumper. Citrus and sweet lime sneak in like a memory. And that chocolate? It lingers like a song you didn’t know you missed. This one doesn't just brew - it   drips  . You’ll want to cancel your plans and call it nostalgia.  
   
   ROAST LEVEL:  Medium Plus    
   PROCESSING:  Washed + Naturals&nbsp;  
   REGION:   Venkids Valley Estate(Karnataka) &  Harley Estate(Karnataka)  
   ALTITUDE:  1200 MASL (metres above sea level)    
   VARIETAL:  SLN 9 + SLN 795     
   HARVEST:  2025    
   BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual (Espresso, Moka Pot, South Indian Filter, Aeropress, French Press)    
   BEVERAGE STYLE:  Cold Brew, Manual Brews, Milk Based Drinks  
   
  Where Raincheck Grows  
    Raincheck   is grown where rain isn't a disruption, it's a rhythm. Two estates, two approaches, one shared respect for water, weather, and waiting for the right moment.  
  At   Venkids Valley Estate  , in the lush hills near Madikeri, nature sets the pace. This 200-acre expanse hums with wild fig, mango, avocado, and soapnut trees. Birds nest, breezes carry song, and coffee grows slowly beneath a dense canopy at 3600 feet. Pavan and Shilpa run the estate with quiet conviction, solar-powered homes, rainwater harvesting, and a community that’s been part of the land for decades. Here, modern machinery meets old-school care, and every bean reflects the patience of a place that listens to the rain.  
  Then there’s   Harley Estate  , further south in Sakleshpur. One of Karnataka’s most storied coffee farms, it balances heritage with innovation. With misty mornings and rich soil, Harley produces washed and natural coffees, and is known for its pioneering work in monsoon processing. Water isn’t just weather here, it’s part of the profile. Beans are aged in precisely controlled conditions, echoing the old shipping-route serendipity of monsooned coffee, but crafted with intention.  
  Together, these estates deliver a cup that’s moody, mellow, and quietly complex.   Raincheck   is for slow sippers and everything worth waiting for.

Name: Troublemaker
Tasting_Notes: Apricot and dark caramel pull you in, but it’s that figgy depth and nutty thump that makes you stay
Desc:
This one? It doesn't ask for permission. Think sweet lime with a side of defiance. Apricot and dark caramel pull you in, but it’s that figgy depth and nutty thump that makes you stay. With milk or straight-up bold - it doesn’t care. It’s for the ones who rewrite the rules while sipping their second cup.  
  ROAST LEVEL : Medium 
   PROCESSING:  Washed + Naturals 
  REGION:   Venkids Valley Estate (Karnataka) &  The Laks Farm (Tamil Nadu) 
  ALTITUDE:  1300 MASL (metres above sea level) 
  VARIETAL:  Chandragiri + SLN 9 + Canephora 
  HARVEST:  2025 
  BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual (French Press, Aeropress, Pour-over, South Indian Filter, Cold Brew) 
  BEVERAGE STYLE:  Cold Brew, Manual Brew, Milk Based Drinks  
  Where The Trouble Brews  
 Troublemaker isn’t born in one place. It comes from two farms, two philosophies, and one shared spirit: do things differently, and do them with intent. 
 First, there’s Venkids Valley Estate, tucked away in the Western Ghats near Madikeri. A winding road leads you in, past rivulets and wild fig trees, into 200 acres of untamed green. Pavan and Shilpa run the show, welcoming, passionate, and quietly rebellious. Here, at 3600 feet, coffee grows under a dense jungle canopy alongside over 40 species of trees. It’s processed with precision, but powered by people, a close-knit team living in solar-powered homes, harvesting rainwater, and keeping the land alive with every step. 
 Then, high in the Pulney Hills of Tamil Nadu, there’s The Laks Farm, nestled in Pachalur village. One of the highest coffee-growing regions in India, it runs on organic principles and deep respect for the ecosystem. No chemicals. No shortcuts. Just a farm where coffee grows with oranges, bananas, cardamom, and pepper, layered in flavor and full of life. 
 Together, these farms bring you a coffee that’s bold, bright, and a little wild. Just like its name. Troublemaker doesn’t play safe. It plays real.

Location – Chikmagalur, Karnataka    Altitude – 1200 Masl    Varietal – Kents    Process – PSD    Cup Notes – Jaggery Bites, Plum, Cocoa    Roast Profile – Medium   Net wt. - 250 g | 8.8 oz   Merthi Subbangudigy Estate (MS Estate) is located in the Sahyadari ranges of the Western Ghats, Chikmagalur, Karnataka. The estate is part of Balanoor Plantations which is run by Mr Ashok Kuriyan and his son Mr Rohan Kuriyan. Arabicas (rain forest certified) are grown under the shade of tress like, Silver Oaks, Dadaps and various jungle woods. Special attention is paid to every aspect of picking, pulping, fermenting, washing, drying and curing. The practice of sustainability and environmental responsibility is the heart of the farm.   About the Process-   The Kents banana leaf psd is a special coffee for us as it's one of the first experiments we did last year which succeeded. The coffee is carefully harvested to ensure only the best cherry is taken for this nano lot. The cherries are pulped trying to retain as much mucilage on the bean before it is dried on the raised beds under fresh banana leaves. The coffee is raked frequently and the leaves changed when it dries. The pulp and the banana leaf give these coffees it's sweet cupping notes.

  Ethiopian Yirgacheffe Grade   1 – Idido  is a floral masterpiece. Grown at high elevations in the Gedeo Zone and washed for clarity, this coffee delivers delicate jasmine, bergamot, and lemon zest notes with a silky tea-like body and crisp acidity. Best brewed as a pour-over or Chemex, it's a favorite for black coffee lovers seeking refined and elegant cups. 
 
 
  Region:   Yirgacheffe, Gedeo Zone, Ethiopia 
 
 
  Elevation:   ~ 1,900–2,100 masl 
 
 
  Processing:   Washed (Grade 1) 
 
 
  Varietals:   Heirloom Ethiopian landraces 
 
 
   Roast Recommendation :  Light to Light-Medium 
 
 
  Cup Style: Delicate, floral, and tea-like  – a clean, elegant cup with bright citrus-laced acidity, silky mouthfeel, and lingering floral aftertaste. This is a quintessential washed Ethiopian profile:  refined, layered, and complex , ideal for slow sips and aroma appreciation.

  Get ready for the ultimate barista experience at home. With a professional chromed brass group and filter holder to ensure a perfect Italian espresso at home. Backed with a new intuitive user interface, a professional steam wand and new body shape that makes the water level visible.  
 The new Gaggia Classic is the culmination of our 80 years of tradition, history, and experience. Stylishly designed and totally made in Italy. 
   
  Brand: Gaggia  
  Usage Type: Home & Offices    
 
 PROFESSIONAL STAINLESS STEEL FILTER-HOLDER  Designed to professional standards, the group head and filter holder are made of Stainless Steel to give you the best in espresso quality and machine longevity. The heavy Stainless Steel filter-holder ensures a consistent and stable brewing temperature throughout the entire brewing process.   SOLENOID VALVE  The three-way solenoid valve relieves the pressure in the filter holder immediately after pulling a shot. Water empties from the filter holder via the open valve, and into the drip tray. This leaves the coffee puck dry, making it easy to clean.   TRADITIONAL GAGGIA BOILER  Polished Aluminium boiler is designed for unparalleled temperature stability, giving you the best espresso every time you brew.   PROFESSIONAL STEAM WAND WITH 2 STEAM OUTLETS  The perfect way to steam the milk, and make exquisitely silky, bar-quality microfoam.

CUP HOLDER   Espresso cups and glasses can be stored on the top of the machine for convenience, and to be ambiently heated by the boiler. Tasting_Notes: Milk Chocolate, Mild Acidity, Balanced Body: Medium
Desc:
Boothangudi Estate | Decaffeinated Coffee | High Altitude Arabica  
  An Experimental Coffee Producer in Chikmagalur, India. This estate is Classified as a "Sacred Grove" that has a special religious and cultural importance. 
 Boothangudi Estate is located at an altitude of 1000-1000 MASL and has a  Perennial water source in the estate feeding the plantation, and as drinking water for the farmers.   
   Boothangudi is named after Lord Boothappan.   A powerful deity in the estate who is meant to protect the estate from natural calamities and keeps the people safe.   Lord Boothappan also ensures timely rains, brings birds, animals and insects to play various roles in balanced flora and fauna.    "Boothan" meaning Lord boothappan & "Gudi" meaning Temple.    Boothangudi is classified as "Sacred Groves" in india dating backing to over 2000 years old.   Every year, people from as far as 900+ kms travel to this place and offer gifts to god and pray for safety and prosperity.  
  This experimental plantation also processes it's high altitude arabicas with a  Honey process which is the most labor intensive, but worth an experiment! The natural stream, perennial water source is very essential for the estate apart from timely rains. It is used for pulping, washing and irrigation purposes. The coffee also undergoes hand garbling to remove twigs, leaves and unripe fruits before the pulping process. Just another highlight of the estate is the Areca Palms providing shades to these juicy arabica cherries year-round!   
   Natural CO2 Decaffeination :   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  Decaffeination is the act of removing caffeine from coffee beans leaving the aroma as it is. It   is carried out while the beans are still ‘green’, before they are roasted  . Drinking decaffeinated coffee is in theory, a way of enjoying the beverage while eliminating the caffeine and preserving the taste.   
 
 
 
 
  Consumer preference for natural, organic, and minimally processed foods is growing dramatically, as we all recognise that a healthy lifestyle includes not only good exercise and nutrition but also the elimination of chemicals and artificial ingredients in our food. We are using Super Critical Co2 fluid extraction process for decaffeination of coffee.  
 
 
 
 
  Benefits of this method:  
 
 
 
 
  ·     Extracts Caffeine effectively. It’s a direct contact method but does not use chemicals  .   ·     Doesn't chemically affect proteins or carbohydrates of the coffee beans.   ·     The byproducts are natural and 100% recyclable.   ·     100% organic process.  
  ·     Green process.

Name: Jura Z10 - Aluminium White - Fully Automatic Coffee Machine

Desc:
Jura Z10 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  Jura Z10, a Coffee Machine designed to perfection for the best coffee experience.  
 
 
 The groundbreaking Z10 with P.R.G. for hot and cold brew specialty coffees 
 
 A masterpiece of Swiss engineering, the new Z10 doubles the range of specialty coffees. At the touch of a button it prepares the full spectrum of hot drinks from intense espresso to on-trend flat white. It also opens up a whole new dimension in the enjoyment of coffee with the introduction of cold brew specialties. This is made possible thanks to the Product Recognizing Grinder (P.R.G.), which recognizes the chosen specialty and instantly and precisely adjusts the fineness of grind accordingly. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 In addition, JURA has developed the pioneering Cold Extraction Process – a quite literally refreshing top innovation. In this process, cold water is slowly pulsed through the freshly ground coffee under high pressure. The result is a completely new way of experiencing coffee – refreshing, energizing and with a wonderfully balanced aroma.  
 This outstanding premium coffee machine features a double-speed 4.3” touch display and the Blue Crystal Rotary Switch. Thanks to the Specialty Selection menu, it's exceptionally easy and intuitive to use. The technological quantum leap is also reflected in the sculptural design. The convex-concave front panel is visible proof of the attention to detail and absolute manufacturing precision. Its high quality makes the Z10 a statement of excellent taste. 
 
 
 
  Brand: Jura  
  Usage Type: Home & Offices  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The new Product Recognizing Grinder (P.R.G.) 
 To ensure the optimum grind for every specialty, JURA engineers developed the Product Recognizing Grinder (P.R.G.). The electronically controlled high-performance grinder adjusts in a fraction of a second to the predefined consistency of grind – much more quickly and frequently than could be done manually. Its spectrum ranges from very fine for short classics to very coarse for long specialties. But coffee lovers don’t need to worry, because the adjustment takes place automatically every time a beverage is prepared and, if preferred, can also be individually selected before each preparation with the Aroma Selection feature.  
 Cold brew – extreme freshness 
 Thanks to the Cold Extraction Process, the Z10 prepares genuine cold brew specialties. While many conventional cold coffee drinks consist mostly of hot-brewed coffee which is then chilled, in the Z10 extraction takes place with cold water, pulsed at high pressure, and more coarsely ground coffee. The end result is a natural, energizing and refreshing beverage in which the fruity aromas of the coffee can be fully enjoyed without being overwhelmed by bitters. Anything else would just be a cold coffee.  
 Eighth-generation brewing unit 
 The brewing unit is the most important part of any automatic coffee machine. For the Z10, JURA has created the eighth-generation brewing unit. With its unique 3D brewing technology, it allows the water to flow evenly through the ground coffee at multiple levels. This makes the most of the aroma, both in hot specialties and with cold brewing.   
 Lasting elegance 
 Design and the careful choice of materials play an important role in product durability. JURA always strives to achieve a design that people will be proud to own and that will still look fresh and modern after many years. Uncompromising quality, durable, high-quality materials and maximum engineering precision guarantee both culinary and aesthetic excellence throughout the lifetime of the machine.  A high-tech two-component method provides the surfaces with an intense sense of depth, so that just looking at the coffee machine is a pleasure in itself. The water tank with its elegant wave design and the harmonious filter casing are just two examples of the attention paid to what might seem like small details. As soon as you touch the Z10, you sense what true worth means to JURA.
[Meta Description]: This outstanding premium coffee machine features a double-speed 4.3” touch display and the Blue Crystal Rotary Switch.

Desc:
Boothangudi Estate | Decaffeinated Coffee | High Altitude Arabica  
  An Experimental Coffee Producer in Chikmagalur, India. This estate is Classified as a "Sacred Grove" that has a special religious and cultural importance. 
 Boothangudi Estate is located at an altitude of 1000-1000 MASL and has a  Perennial water source in the estate feeding the plantation, and as drinking water for the farmers.   
   Boothangudi is named after Lord Boothappan.   A powerful deity in the estate who is meant to protect the estate from natural calamities and keeps the people safe.   Lord Boothappan also ensures timely rains, brings birds, animals and insects to play various roles in balanced flora and fauna.    "Boothan" meaning Lord boothappan & "Gudi" meaning Temple.    Boothangudi is classified as "Sacred Groves" in india dating backing to over 2000 years old.   Every year, people from as far as 900+ kms travel to this place and offer gifts to god and pray for safety and prosperity.  
  This experimental plantation also processes it's high altitude arabicas with a  Honey process which is the most labor intensive, but worth an experiment! The natural stream, perennial water source is very essential for the estate apart from timely rains. It is used for pulping, washing and irrigation purposes. The coffee also undergoes hand garbling to remove twigs, leaves and unripe fruits before the pulping process. Just another highlight of the estate is the Areca Palms providing shades to these juicy arabica cherries year-round!   
   Natural CO2 Decaffeination :   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  Decaffeination is the act of removing caffeine from coffee beans leaving the aroma as it is. It   is carried out while the beans are still ‘green’, before they are roasted  . Drinking decaffeinated coffee is in theory, a way of enjoying the beverage while eliminating the caffeine and preserving the taste.   
 
 
 
 
  Consumer preference for natural, organic, and minimally processed foods is growing dramatically, as we all recognise that a healthy lifestyle includes not only good exercise and nutrition but also the elimination of chemicals and artificial ingredients in our food. We are using Super Critical Co2 fluid extraction process for decaffeination of coffee.  
 
 
 
 
  Benefits of this method:  
 
 
 
 
  ·     Extracts Caffeine effectively. It’s a direct contact method but does not use chemicals  .   ·     Doesn't chemically affect proteins or carbohydrates of the coffee beans.   ·     The byproducts are natural and 100% recyclable.   ·     100% organic process.  
  ·     Green process.

  Estate Information - Ponnathmotte Estate  
 A 20 km drive from the scenic Madikeri town of the Coorg district in Karnataka leads you to the sprawling Ponnathmotte Estate, where the rich aroma of coffee beans engulfs you. The word ‘Ponnathmotte’ means ‘Golden Hills’ in the local language. The estate was started over 80 years ago and is now looked after by the owners’ third generation. The region is blessed with adequate rainfall, rich soil, and an ideal climate suited to growing coffee. 
 Thanks to its elevation of 3,600 ft. (1,100 m), Ponnathmotte Estate produces superior quality of Robusta & Arabica coffee seeds, as well as a special blend of hybrid variety known as CxR(Coffea congenisis and Robusta) . The estate’s immense tree canopy attracts a wide variety of migratory birds from long distances and provides a natural habitat for insects and honeybees. These factors help in better cross-pollination thus increasing the yield of Robusta. Also, thanks to the natural farming techniques employed, the coffee beans produced meet the highest quality standards. 
 Another specialty is the good number of rosewood trees that thrive in the estate and provide filter shade which is necessary for coffee plants. Cluster fig trees can be seen as well around the plantation, which not only provide shade, but its fruit cultivation is known to improve the coffee taste. Ponnathmotte Estate employs a full-time labour force who are provided individual quarters within the estate. The estate also grows other spices such as cardamom, pepper, and a few selections of fruits.

 A 20 km drive from the scenic Madikeri town of the Coorg district in Karnataka leads you to the sprawling Ponnathmotte Estate, where the rich aroma of coffee beans engulfs you. The word ‘Ponnathmotte’ means ‘Golden Hills’ in the local language. The estate was started over 80 years ago and is now looked after by the owners’ third generation. The region is blessed with adequate rainfall, rich soil, and an ideal climate suited to growing coffee.Thanks to its elevation of 3,600 ft. (1,100 m), Ponnathmotte Estate produces superior quality of Robusta & Arabica coffee seeds, as well as a special blend of hybrid variety known as CxR (Coffea congenisis and Robusta)The estate’s immense tree canopy attracts a wide variety of migratory birds from long distances and provides a natural habitat for insects and honeybees. 
 These factors help in better cross-pollination thus increasing the yield of Robusta. Also, thanks to the natural farming techniques employed, the coffee beans produced meet the highest quality standards. Another specialty is the good number of rosewood trees that thrive in the estate and provide filter shade which is necessary for coffee plants. Cluster fig trees can be seen as well around the plantation, which not only provide shade, but its fruit cultivation is known to improve the coffee taste. Ponnathmotte Estate employs a full-time labour force who are provided individual quarters within the estate. The estate also grows other spices such as cardamom, pepper, and a few selections of fruits.

Name: Southern Express | Medium-Dark Roast Coffee
Tasting_Notes: Smooth
Desc:

Name: Bialetti Moka Espresso | 2 Cups
Desc:
Moka Pot is compact brewing machine for a concentrated dose of coffee. Intensely flavoured, aromatic and full bodied it’s a perfect reminiscence of an espresso.  
  The pressurized brewing technique brews a strong, rich coffee, mostly at the right temperature. Available in Aluminium or stainless steel, choose one to fit your stove or pick one with an induction base across varying capacities to fit your need.  
   
  The stovetop espresso maker can be found in almost every Italian home. With a stovetop espresso maker you can make coffee that is very close to the traditional Italian style espresso coffee. The result is an intense, strong coffee full of flavour, and the coffee is also a good base for specialty milk coffees such as cappuccinos.   Color:  Silver

Name: Authentic South Indian Brass Coffee Filter
Desc:
Bring back the ritual of slow, measured, unhurried filter coffee into your everyday. Made of solid brass, our Filter Set is designed the way it has been for generations. With simplicity. Use it to extract thick, strong, aromatic decoction from your coffee and pour it into a tumbler with intention. 
  Why Brass  
 Brass has always been part of traditional South Indian kitchens. It holds heat well, ages beautifully, and adds a certain weight to the process. It’s something you can feel in your hands every morning. 
  What’s Included  
 
 Upper chamber (for coffee powder) 
 Lower chamber (to collect decoction) 
 Press disc 
 Lid 
 
  Care Instructions  
 
 Wash gently with mild soap 
 Dry immediately to avoid water marks 
 Over time, brass may naturally darken 
 Polish occasionally if you prefer a brighter finish

Desc:
We have a new honey process coffee and it's extra sweet! 
 Sourced from Krishnagiri estate ,high up in the Chandra drona hills(a.k.a the Giris) of Chikmagalur, this particular lot fascinated us with its sweetness and lingering fruitiness.

Name: Hamsanādam
Tasting_Notes: There is oodles of milk chocolate sweetness that is punctuated by a lemon candy like acidity and marigold florals
Process: ing is a simple traditional washed
Desc:
We have a new washed coffee and it's a revelation! 
  Perumpallam is a village on the northern  side of the lower Kodaikanal hills. The high altitude of the place is very conducive for growing complex arabicas.  
 We have been fascinated by how complex the Kodaikanal region is as a coffee growing area and have been especially curious about  the higher elevation small holder farms there. 
  The good folks at Ram estate helped us procure this interesting community arabica lot from Perumpallam. The varietal is chandragiri and the processing is a simple traditional washed. This simplicity allows the plant care and the terroir to really shine in the cup. 
  We took our time dialling in the roast of this lot but once we figured out a profile that worked, the cup really started to shine. There is oodles of milk chocolate sweetness that is punctuated by a lemon candy like acidity and marigold florals. The coffee does take some time to peak but once there we also started noticing raspberry like fruitiness too!  This complex effervescence reminded our roaster of the rāga hamsanādam. 
 Hamsanādam the coffee is a delight across all manual brews but especially the v60 , 12 days post date of roast. It also makes for a more-ish shot of espresso 24 days post date of roast! We hope to source more frequently from this high altitude corner of the Kodaikanal hills!

Name: Mind=blown (redux)
Tasting_Notes: We taste very prominent peach and green grapes in the acidity that is balanced really well with a vanilla-eque sweetness
Desc:
OG best seller is back again and this time it's a light roast! We always ask the good folks at Mooleh Manay for more coffee when we run out of mind=blown. This season, they obliged! 
  This is the same coffee as what was launched earlier, so the processing details are the same . The good folks at Mooleh Manay wanted  to up the complexity of this year's lot while maintaining the consistency they achieved last year. To do this, they decided to throw the kitchen sink at the coffee in the processing department by using a custom yeast  culture along with carbonic maceration. 
  The start of the intricate process is by picking ripe arabica cherries(mix of Sln6, Sln 9 and Chandragiri) and using a syphon tank to remove immature cherries that float. 
  The sunken cherries are then pre dried for 48 hours. This is a very important step as it reduces the moisture, which helps achieve better control in the fermentation. This goes a long way to prevent any off flavours. 
  The pre-dried cherries are then put in sealed barrels along with a custom yeast culture and a controlled carbonic maceration enviornment is created. The fermentation lasts for 60 hours. 
  The cherries are then dried in a poly house for 10 days, where they are raked constantly to ensure even drying. 
  This extensive and intricate process has resulted in a coffee that is a revelation! Since we were sent this bag a couple of months ago, we wanted to do something different to highlight what the coffee has to offer. After much experimentation we settled in on a light roast profile that minimises bitterness and maximises the acidity. We taste very prominent peach and green grapes  in the acidity that is balanced really well with a vanilla-eque sweetness. This coffee is a real  delight on a manual brew(we prefer a v60) with really vibrant  acidity, good sweetness and next to no bitterness even when extraction is pushed. 
  The coffee really opens up 12days post roast date for manual brews and makes for a fruit jam of an espresso 20 days post roast date. This coffee is not be missed on any count!

Name: Nalinakānti
Tasting_Notes: lychee with a lingering raisin like sweetness and a subtle rosewater undercurrent which we find very refreshing
Desc:
Last season's hit from Ram estate is back! 
 Located in the village of Kamanur near Thandigudi, Ram estate (called Rothaikadu by locals ) posseses a unique microclimate that is idealfor growing complex arabicas  and the folks there  have been processing top notch coffees from year one of their foray into the  speciality scene. 
   This particular lot consists only of  selectively picked SLN 09 arabica from the estate's highest portion. We had a hand in fine tuning the processing this lot and we thank Ram estate for listening to our suggestions. While the total fermentation time was 160 hrs, this was split between pre and post pulping. The cherries were fermented in a steel barrel with CO2 being pumped in. They were then taken out, pulped and then fermented again in similar conditionstill a total time of 160 hrs was reached.  
   The resulting cup is very aromatic ,very  tropical  and very sweet, but also shockingly 'clean' tasting ; without much fermenty notes. This is party a result of the aforementioned microclimate and partly because of careful monitoring of the cherries during fermentation and the slow drying.  The acidity tastes of lychee with a lingering raisin like sweetness and a subtle rosewater undercurrent which we find very refreshing, like the rāga nalinakānti. 
 Nalinakānti the coffee is a very sweet , complex, sippable brew  and is a delight across all manual brew methods 10 days post roasting. It makes a fruity shot of espresso 20 days post date of roast.

Desc:

Name: Baarbara Estate - Honey Sundried Processed
Tasting_Notes: Expect a bright, fruity aroma with notes of berries , a rounded body , and a lingering sweetness
Desc:
Baarbara Estate – Honey Processed Arabica   Single Origin | Medium Roast | Limited Estate Release  
 Nestled in the misty heights of the Western Ghats,  Baarbara Estate  is a third-generation coffee plantation run by the  Indavara family , proud cultivators of coffee since  1896  under  MG Plantations . With over 120 years of heritage and a deep-rooted commitment to sustainability, the estate is certified by both  UTZ  and the  Rainforest Alliance . 
 At elevations ranging from  3,850 to 5,350 feet , this estate produces exceptional  Selection 795 Arabica , shade-grown in rich biodiversity. The result is a coffee that truly reflects the unique terroir of  Chikmagalur , near the sacred foothills of  Bababudan Giri  India’s coffee cradle. 
 At Korebi Coffee, we collaborate closely with estates like Baarbara to  develop a roast that captures the estate’s unique character and natural expression . This year’s release is a  Honey Processed  lot, using a time-intensive and flavor-rich technique. 
 ☀️ About the Honey Sun-Dried Process: 
 In the  honey process , freshly pulped beans are  left with some of their sticky mucilage intact  and then  sun-dried on raised beds . This method named for the golden, honey-like texture of the drying beans enhances the coffee’s  natural sweetness and fruity depth , while preserving the  clarity and balance  of a washed coffee. It’s a labor of love that results in a cup with exceptional character. 
 ☕ Tasting Notes: 
 Expect a  bright, fruity aroma  with notes of  berries , a  rounded body , and a  lingering sweetness . The  medium roast  preserves the vibrant complexity of the honey process while delivering a smooth, balanced finish. 
  Key Features:  
 
 
  100% Arabica | Single Origin | Shade Grown  
 
 
  Honey Sun-Dried for Sweet, Fruit-Forward Notes  
 
 
  Ethically Sourced | UTZ & Rainforest Alliance Certified  
 
 
  Handpicked at High Elevation (3850–5350 ft)  
 
 
  Available as Whole Bean or Freshly Ground  
 
 
 Perfect for those who seek  sweet, nuanced, and expertly processed coffee ,  Baarbara Estate – Honey Processed  is a standout in our estate collection and a true expression of Indian specialty coffee done right.
